summary: The International Chinese Language Teachers Scholarship is run by the Center for Language Education and Cooperation (CLEC) in China. Confucius Institutes, approved HSK test centres, foreign universities, professional associations and Chinese embassies or consulates abroad recommend outstanding students and in-service Chinese language teachers, who then study international Chinese language education and related subjects at a Chinese host university. Study can be a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree, or a non-degree programme of up to 11 months, 5 months or 4 weeks. The scholarship supports tuition, accommodation, a monthly living allowance (not for four-week students) and medical insurance.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens who are friendly to China, have no criminal record, obey Chinese law and the host university's rules, and are in good physical and mental health with good academic and behavioural standing. They must be interested in Chinese language education and related work, and a recommending institution must put them forward.

Age: between 16 and 35 on 1 September 2026; in-service Chinese language teachers may be up to 45. Bachelor's applicants are generally under 25 (BLCU).

Entry level and language, as stated for the September 2026 intake. Doctoral: master's degree in teaching Chinese as a foreign language, linguistics, international Chinese language education or a related field, HSK Level 6 with at least 200 and HSKK Advanced at least 60 (BLCU also accepts HSK 7 passing). Master's: bachelor's degree, HSK Level 5 with at least 210 and HSKK Intermediate at least 60. Bachelor's: senior high school diploma, HSK Level 4 with at least 210 and HSKK Intermediate at least 60, plus a valid CSCA score report (BLCU). One-year study: International Chinese Language Education needs HSK Level 3 at least 270 and an HSKK score; Chinese Language and Literature (also History or Philosophy) needs HSK Level 4 at least 180 and HSKK Intermediate at least 60; Chinese Language Study needs HSK Level 3 at least 210, with priority for an HSKK score. One-semester study: HSK Level 3 at least 180 and an HSKK score for language, literature, history or philosophy tracks; Traditional Chinese Medicine and Taiji culture tracks need an HSK score, with priority for HSKK. Four-week study: an HSK score.

Priority goes to degree applicants who can show an employment contract with a teaching institution after their studies, or equivalent proof, and to in-service teachers with proof of employment and an employer's recommendation. In principle, someone who received a similar scholarship in the past three years is not admitted to the one-semester or one-year programme. An applicant may hold only one Chinese government scholarship; multiple applications are invalid. SYSU requires a bachelor's degree for its master's route and applicants 18 to 35.
age_experience_notes: Age 16 to 35 on 1 September 2026; in-service Chinese language teachers up to 45 (SYSU states 18 to 35 for its master's). Bachelor's applicants are generally under 25. In-service teachers must show proof of employment and an employer's recommendation letter. No other work experience is required.
funding_summary: The scholarship supports tuition, accommodation, a living allowance and comprehensive medical insurance. Tuition is used by the host university to teach and manage scholars, run cultural activities and HSK tests. Free on-campus accommodation is usually a double room; a scholar approved to live off campus gets RMB 700 per month (RMB 1,000 for doctoral students). Monthly allowance in the CLEC standard: RMB 2,500 for undergraduates and for one-year and one-semester students, RMB 3,000 for master's students and RMB 3,500 for doctoral students; four-week students get no allowance. Insurance premium: RMB 100 (four weeks), RMB 400 (one semester), RMB 800 per year (longer). Length: bachelor's up to 4 academic years, master's up to 2, doctoral up to 4, one-year up to 11 months, one-semester up to 5 months, four-week programme 4 weeks.
programmes_note: Programmes read: doctoral, master's and bachelor's degrees in International Chinese Language Education (the bachelor's is Chinese Language and Literature with an international Chinese language education focus at BLCU); one-year study in International Chinese Language Education, Chinese Language and Literature (also Chinese History or Chinese Philosophy at Beihang) or Chinese Language Study; one-semester study in the same fields plus Traditional Chinese Medicine and Taiji culture; four-week study in Chinese Language Study, Traditional Chinese Medicine, Taiji culture or Chinese language plus a Chinese family stay. The CLEC guide also lists joint-programme scholarships (funded with universities or education departments) and online programmes (one-year or one-semester Chinese Language Study; tuition only). Course listings come from the host university.
institutions_note: Applicants register with the CLEC scholarship platform, choose a recommending institution and a host institution, and study at the host. CLEC's 2026 platform lists 236 host institutions, with different ones for trainee (non-degree), undergraduate, master's and doctoral study; the table could not be split by level when read. Hosts read: Beijing Language and Culture University, Beihang University, Sun Yat-sen University. Recommenders: Confucius Institutes and independent Confucius Classrooms, selected HSK test centres, foreign educational institutions, Chinese teacher-training programmes or Chinese departments at foreign universities, professional Chinese-teaching associations, and Chinese embassies or consulates abroad.

requirements.text: Scanned passport photo page. Passport valid until at least 1 December 2026 and a profile photo (SYSU).
Scanned HSK and HSKK score reports within their two-year validity, at the level the programme needs.
Reference letter from the head of the recommending institution.
Certificate of the highest diploma or proof of expected graduation; an expected graduate must give the formal diploma before registering (BLCU). SYSU asks for CHSI or CSCSE verification.
Official transcripts for every semester of the highest study.
Two reference letters from professors, associate professors or experts of equivalent title.

Master's: study plan of over 800 Chinese characters (BLCU), or over 3,000 words covering background, research, study and career plans (SYSU). Doctoral: 3,000-word personal statement in Chinese with the intended research field and a research proposal.
Acceptance letter from the intended supervisor (BLCU).
Valid CSCA score report obtained before the deadline (BLCU).
Proof of employment and a reference letter from the employer.
Notarised guardianship statement signed by a guardian (BLCU: a non-Chinese citizen living in China or a Chinese citizen living in Beijing).
Foreigner Physical Examination Form with chest X-ray, ECG and lab results, hospital-stamped and dated within six months (SYSU).
Non-criminal record certificate from local authorities within six months before submission (SYSU).
Additional documents required by the host university; attendance at the host's interview where one is held (Beihang, SYSU).

application_steps.title: Find a recommending institution and host university
application_steps.detail: Applicants must be put forward by a recommending institution such as a Confucius Institute, an approved HSK centre, a foreign university or a Chinese embassy or consulate. They then choose a host institution and check its admission criteria and deadlines. Chinese Bridge winners with a scholarship certificate send their documents, with the certificate, straight to the host through the scholarship platform.

application_steps.title: Register and apply on the CLEC scholarship platform
application_steps.detail: Online registration opened on 1 March in 2026 (and in the 2024 edition). Applicants search for institutions, submit materials online and track their application. Deadlines in Beijing time for the 2026 round: 15 April for July programmes, 15 May for September, 15 September for December, and 31 October 2026 for March 2027. Recommending and host institutions finish their review about ten days later.

application_steps.title: Apply to the host and submit signed forms
application_steps.detail: Some hosts need a second application. SYSU requires an account in its own application system, the signed application and commitment forms and a printed, hand-signed CLEC form. Beihang and SYSU invite applicants to an interview.

application_steps.title: Review by the host and an expert panel
application_steps.detail: The recommending institution and the host review the application, then CLEC asks an expert panel to review. Decisions are based on HSK and HSKK levels and scores, geographical distribution and other factors. Degree applicants with a teaching employment contract after study, and in-service teachers with proof, get priority.

application_steps.title: Results about three months before the start
application_steps.detail: Results are announced about three months before the programme starts. SYSU issues notices on a rolling basis and the final scholarship admission depends on the CLEC expert review. Applicants who got a similar scholarship in the past three years are in principle not admitted to one-semester or one-year programmes.

application_steps.title: Confirm the arrangements and register
application_steps.detail: Selected applicants confirm the study arrangements with the host, print the scholarship certificate online, and register on the date in the Letter of Admission. Registration after the stated period cancels the scholarship, and a pre-enrolment medical examination must be passed.

application_steps.title: Annual assessment and continuing conditions
application_steps.detail: Degree students take part in an annual assessment (SYSU: result full, partial or suspended scholarship). A scholar who withdraws early, suspends studies or does not register without permission loses the scholarship, and false documents or hidden visa records lead to cancellation.
